statement: For A={0,1,2} with operation table rows (0,0,0), (1,0,1), (1,1,1), and every finite nonempty fixed label set I, two full linear binary terms on I (each variable once, arbitrary order, no constants) induce the same function A^I -> A if and only if their leftmost-decomposition trees agree as rooted labelled trees with exactly one distinguished child at each nonleaf and all other children unordered. Every such decorated tree is realised. Hence for every n>=1 the number c_n of these term functions is (n-1)! times the sum, for k=0,...,n-1, of binom(n,k) k^(n-1-k)/(n-1-k)!, with 0^0=1. Equivalently T(x)=sum_{n>=1}c_n x^n/n! satisfies T=x(1+T exp(T)); a direct integer recurrence and a function-only recursive decoder are supplied. This resolves the exact all-n counting question in source.md at its frozen interpretation in problem.md.
contribution: Proposed complete resolution of the SC229 associative-commutative spectrum question explicitly posed by Huang and Lehtonen (2024), Section 7. The new component is injective all-arity reconstruction of the root, distinguished child, and ordinary children from disjoint AND-prime factors of the term function, including singleton indicators. Earlier leftmost-tree methods and standard labelled enumeration are attributed, and no novelty is claimed for them in isolation. No equivalent SC229 result was found in the documented bounded primary-source search on 2026-09-12; universal priority is not claimed. This is a candidate requesting fresh mathematical review, not an acceptance.
